title: EduData Saver
tagline: Students and families are hit by high mobile data costs and confusing billing

marketGap: No dedicated service aggregates bulk data purchases and offers zero‑rated bundles specifically for education, leaving learners to pay retail rates and deal with opaque billing.
executionPlan: Launch an MVP web/app that partners with major Nigerian telecoms to buy bulk data at wholesale rates and resell discounted, zero‑rated packages for approved educational platforms. title: Microgrid‑as‑a‑Service for Nigerian SMEs
tagline: Frequent blackouts are draining small business revenues and forcing costly diesel generators
whyNow: Nigeria’s chronic grid failures have intensified after the latest six‑year blackout in Oke‑Ogun and the government’s new power‑control centre has yet to restore reliable supply, creating immediate demand for dependable electricity solutions for cash‑strapped SMEs.

proof.text: Businesses report erratic power supply causing losses of up to 30% of daily revenue and forcing them to run expensive diesel generators.
Residents of Oke‑Ogun have been living under a six‑year blackout and are pleading with IBEDC and Governor Makinde to restore power, highlighting the depth of the supply crisis.
The federal government has launched a new power control centre aimed at curbing blackouts, but implementation delays mean businesses remain without reliable electricity.

marketGap: No affordable, subscription‑based microgrid service exists that aggregates solar, battery and diesel backup to deliver uninterrupted power specifically for small retailers, workshops and kiosks in blackout‑prone Nigerian towns.
executionPlan: Launch an MVP microgrid hub in Oke‑Ogun serving 20‑30 nearby SMEs with a pay‑per‑kilowatt‑hour subscription model; partner with local solar installers for hardware, use a cloud‑based energy‑management platform to monitor usage and billing; monetize through monthly subscriptions and a small margin on excess energy sold to the grid.
competitor: None offers a turnkey, subscription‑based microgrid tailored to SMEs in Nigeria; closest alternatives are standalone solar home systems (e.g., SolarNow) and diesel generator rentals.
trend: Decentralised renewable energy and digital payment platforms are rapidly scaling across Africa, making on‑demand micro‑power services both technically feasible and financially attractive.

title: Rural Lung Diagnostic Hub

marketGap: There is no affordable point‑of‑care lung function testing device coupled with a tele‑consult platform for Kenya’s remote clinics, leaving patients to travel long distances for basic diagnostics.
executionPlan: Develop an MVP that pairs a low‑cost handheld spirometer with a mobile app that securely transmits results to a network of pulmonologists for remote interpretation. competitor: None currently offers an integrated portable spirometry‑plus‑tele‑consult solution in Kenya; the closest alternatives are generic telemedicine platforms such as mPharma, which focus on pharmacy services rather than lung diagnostics.
trend: Rapid mobile‑health adoption and increasing health‑tech investment across Africa make remote diagnostic hubs both feasible and timely.
